title: Modifying van der Waals Materials via Cavity Vacuum Fluctuations
authors: Mohammad Hassan, Cankut Tasci, Leonardo A. Cunha, Johannes Flick
abstract: In the field of cavity quantum materials, vacuum fluctuations of optical cavities are used for modifying ground-state properties of quantum materials without external driving. Here, one example is the van der Waals (vdW)/dispersion interaction in layered 2D vdW materials, where non-additive long-range correlations can dominate the interlayer binding. While cavity-induced changes of such interactions have been predicted and described using ab initio methods for molecular systems, no efficient description exists yet for extended materials. In this Letter, we close this gap by introducing a periodic formulation of the photon many-body dispersion (pMBD) functional within quantum electrodynamical density-functional theory (QEDFT). Applying this method with efficient $\textbf{q}$-point sampling to bilayer hBN and graphene, we predict cavity-modified stacking, increased equilibrium interlayer distances, and softened layer breathing modes with increasing light-matter coupling strength. Our results establish cavity vacuum fluctuations as a tuning knob for the structural properties of vdW materials.
summary: This paper develops a novel theoretical method using QEDFT to incorporate cavity vacuum fluctuations into the description of vdW materials. By applying this to bilayer hBN and graphene, the authors demonstrate that these vacuum fields can tune structural properties, such as interlayer spacing and stacking preference. This establishes cavity vacuum fluctuations as a powerful, non-invasive control mechanism for quantum materials.
main_problem: The study addresses how vacuum fluctuations from optical cavities can modify the ground-state structural properties of van der Waals (vdW) materials without requiring external driving fields.
main_result: The authors predict that cavity vacuum fluctuations act as a tunable knob, causing cavity-modified stacking, increasing equilibrium interlayer distances, and softening layer breathing modes in materials like hBN and graphene.
method: They introduce a periodic formulation of the photon many-body dispersion (pMBD) functional within the Quantum Electrodynamical Density-Functional Theory (QEDFT) framework.
model_or_system: The system involves layered 2D vdW materials, specifically bilayer hBN and graphene. The theory models the interaction using a Hamiltonian adapted for periodic boundary conditions in reciprocal space (q-space).
key_observables: Binding curves, cavity-mediated energy ($\Delta 	ext{Exc}$), equilibrium interlayer distances, and layer breathing mode (LBM) frequencies.
important_parameters: Light-matter coupling strength ($\lambda$), cavity frequency ($\omega$), and the momentum transfer point (focusing on the $\Gamma$-point, $q=0$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes a periodic solid on a supercell and simplifies the calculation by assuming the cavity primarily influences the $\Gamma$-point ($q=0$).
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows binding curves for hBN and graphene under different coupling strengths. Figure 2 illustrates the predicted expansion of interlayer distance and softening of LBM frequencies as the coupling strength increases.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework (QEDFT/pMBD) to calculate cavity-modified interactions, applies this method to bilayer hBN and graphene, and presents quantitative results showing structural changes dependent on the coupling strength.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges quantum optics (cavity vacuum fluctuations) with condensed matter structure (vdW materials), providing a theoretical tool to engineer material properties using fundamental quantum field effects, which is highly relevant to AMO physics.
